I have been farming these 20 mu for 25 years, and I know every piece of this land. My husband works in the city, and my son and daughter-in-law also go out to work sometimes, so I am the one who mostly takes care of the fields. I have well water, which is good, but pumping costs electricity, so I do not water more than I have to.

For wheat, I always plant improved variety seeds. Last year I used about 25 jin of seed per mu. I bought two bags of compound fertilizer for every mu at sowing time — that is 100 jin per mu of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer. Then in spring, when the wheat is turning green and standing up, I spread another 40 jin of urea per mu. I irrigate four times: once right after sowing to get the seeds going, once before winter so the wheat does not freeze, once at jointing when it is shooting up, and once when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide three times — once for weeds right after sowing, and twice in spring when the bugs and rust start coming. I rotary till before planting wheat to break up the soil. Last year I got about 500 kg per mu, and this year I will do the same. I would rather put a bit more fertilizer than risk losing yield. A bad year means losing real money.

For maize, I plant right after the wheat comes out in June. I use hybrid seed, about 3 jin per mu. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, and then at the big trumpet stage I put another 50 jin of urea per mu. I water three times: after sowing if it is dry, at the jointing stage, and when the grain is filling. Maize drinks a lot when the ears are developing. I spray three times too — herbicide at the beginning, and then insecticide twice because the corn borers and armyworms come every year. I do not till much for maize, just plant right into the wheat stubble with a no-till planter to save time and labor. Last year I got about 550 kg per mu. This year I will try for the same. My neighbor Lao Wang uses about the same amounts, and his crops always look good, so I follow what he does.

I watch my costs. Every jin of fertilizer is money. But I have 20 mu, so I can buy in bulk and get a better price from the dealer. If I spend more on fertilizer, I might cut back on hired labor, but I cannot skip fertilizer — that is the one thing that always pays back.
